sn.s: Un compañero del trabajo se va.
sn.e: A workmate is leaving.

sn.s: Se va para Costa Rica.
sn.e: He is going to Costa Rica.

sn.s: Lo dice un martes, sin aviso.
sn.e: He says it on a Tuesday, with no warning.

sn.s: "Me voy el domingo", dice él.
sn.e: "I'm going on Sunday," he says.

sn.s: Nadie se sorprende mucho.
sn.e: Nobody is very surprised.

sn.s: Aquí siempre hay alguien yéndose.
sn.e: Here there is always somebody leaving.

sn.s: Le preguntan si tiene papeles.
sn.e: They ask him if he has papers.

sn.s: Dice que no, que va a probar.
sn.e: He says no, that he is going to try.

sn.s: Le preguntan si tiene a alguien allá.
sn.e: They ask if he has anybody there.

sn.s: Dice que un primo lo espera en la frontera.
sn.e: He says a cousin is waiting for him at the border.

sn.s: Nadie le dice que no se vaya.
sn.e: Nobody tells him not to go.

sn.s: Nadie le dice que se cuide, tampoco.
sn.e: Nobody tells him to look after himself either.

sn.s: Le hablan del trabajo que hay allá.
sn.e: They talk to him about the work there.

sn.s: Le dicen cuánto se paga en la construcción.
sn.e: They tell him what construction pays.

sn.s: Le dicen dónde se alquila barato.
sn.e: They tell him where you can rent cheap.

sn.s: Le dan datos, no consejos.
sn.e: They give him information, not advice.

sn.s: Eso me llama la atención.
sn.e: That strikes me.

sn.s: Después entiendo por qué es así.
sn.e: Later I understand why it is like that.

sn.s: Ya está decidido.
sn.e: It is already decided.

sn.s: Decirle algo triste no ayuda a nadie.
sn.e: Saying something sad helps nobody.

sn.s: El viernes le hacemos una despedida chiquita.
sn.e: On Friday we give him a small send-off.

sn.s: Compramos cerveza en la pulpería.
sn.e: We buy beer at the pulpería.

sn.s: Nos sentamos afuera del trabajo.
sn.e: We sit outside work.

sn.s: Nadie hace un discurso.
sn.e: Nobody makes a speech.

sn.s: Nadie dice que lo va a extrañar.
sn.e: Nobody says they are going to miss him.

sn.s: Hablan de béisbol casi toda la noche.
sn.e: They talk about baseball nearly all night.

sn.s: Al final Marcos le da la mano.
sn.e: At the end Marcos shakes his hand.

sn.s: "Que le vaya bien, hermano", dice él.
sn.e: "May it go well for you, hermano," he says.

sn.s: Y eso es toda la despedida.
sn.e: And that is the whole goodbye.

sn.s: Le pregunto a Marcos por qué es tan corta.
sn.e: I ask Marcos why it is so short.

sn.s: "Porque si es larga, uno llora", dice él.
sn.e: "Because if it's long, somebody cries," he says.

sn.s: "Y llorando no se va nadie tranquilo."
sn.e: "And crying, nobody leaves calm."

sn.s: El domingo se va con una maleta.
sn.e: On Sunday he leaves with one suitcase.

sn.s: Una maleta para una vida entera.
sn.e: One suitcase for a whole life.

sn.s: Su mamá lo acompaña hasta el bus.
sn.e: His mother goes with him as far as the bus.

sn.s: Eso me lo cuentan después.
sn.e: They tell me that afterwards.

sn.s: Que ella no lloró hasta que el bus arrancó.
sn.e: That she did not cry until the bus pulled away.

sn.s: Y que después lloró toda la tarde.
sn.e: And that then she cried all afternoon.

sn.s: Dos meses después manda un mensaje.
sn.e: Two months later he sends a message.

sn.s: Llegó bien y está trabajando.
sn.e: He arrived safely and is working.

sn.s: Manda una foto de una casa a medio construir.
sn.e: He sends a photo of a half-built house.

sn.s: Ahí trabaja y ahí duerme.
sn.e: He works there and sleeps there.

sn.s: El grupo lo lee en el trabajo.
sn.e: The group reads it at work.

sn.s: Todos dicen que está bien, que le fue bien.
sn.e: Everybody says he is fine, that it went well for him.

sn.s: Y nadie dice lo que todos están pensando.
sn.e: And nobody says what everybody is thinking.

sn.s: Que a lo mejor no vuelve nunca.
sn.e: That maybe he will never come back.
